correctness.rationale: The formal logarithm has exact coefficient \(p^{a-r}/u\), and scaling by \(m\) gives exact valuation \(s+a-r\). For every \(j\) at least two, Legendre factorial bounds force the nonlinear exponential summands into \(p^{s+a+1}\)-divisible series under the stated prime-dependent thresholds, so no higher coefficient can cancel its leading unit. The independent integer recurrence verified 12,900 coefficients in eight parameter sets; the proof itself is symbolic.
